page: Amazon Web Services c7i-flex.8xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual machine powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features 32 vCPUs and 16 physical cores based on the x86_64 architecture, utilizing an Intel Xeon 8488C processor running at 3.2 GHz. The system is equipped with 64.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 5 GHz, providing a memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying entirely on network-attached storage.

Benchmark data shows strong performance in single-threaded operations, with a Geekbench single-core score of 2074.0 and a static web serving throughput of 51.12 GB/sec. The processor includes advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX), which support accelerated matrix and vector calculations. Multi-core performance is characterized by a Geekbench multi-core score of 15951.0 and a multi-threaded bzip3 decompression rate of 111.1 GB/sec. Memory bandwidth reaches 2625.73 GB/sec for cached small-block reads, dropping to 162.39 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads.

The c7i-flex.8xlarge offers a cost-efficient profile for compute-heavy workloads that do not require the full resource allocation of standard c7i instances. The 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio makes it highly suitable for compute-bound tasks such as batch processing, web serving, and moderate database operations. However, the lack of local NVMe storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 6 Gbps represent key tradeoffs for I/O-intensive applications. This configuration is best suited for distributed microservices, software compilation, and medium-scale LLM inference tasks.
